bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced AddressSanitizer's `global-buffer-overflow READ 1` in `lex_multiline_string` on the staged vulnerable checkout at commit `3289a66db7145c081ff1d5fa987f0cfec0563dc5`. The saved witness file is 70,642 bytes, but the fuzz harness clamps `size` to `sizeof(static_data) == 32768` and copies only the first 32,768 bytes into global `static_data` without appending a terminator. Direct inspection of that copied prefix shows bytes 0..2 are `'''`, there is no `0x00` byte anywhere in bytes 0..32767, the only in-prefix `'''` occurs at offset 0, and the last copied byte `static_data[32767]` is `0x0b`. `config_init_data()` then seeds the lexer with `pos = start = static_data` and `end = static_data + 32768`, so the multiline-string lexer sees the full array as its logical span. `lex_config()` recognizes the opening triple single quote and transfers control to `lex_multiline_string()`, which skips the opener and then repeatedly tests `strncmp(lexer->pos, "'''", 3)` before the loop condition `next(lexer) != '\0'`. Because there is no in-bounds closing `'''` and no NUL byte, the condition call from the iteration at `lexer->pos == static_data + 32767` reads the last in-bounds byte `0x0b`, increments `lexer->pos` to `static_data + 32768`, and returns nonzero. The next loop body executes `strncmp(lexer->pos, "'''", 3)` with `lexer->pos` already at the first byte past `static_data`, producing the saved global-buffer-overflow read. The staged patch mitigates the fuzzing path by calling `config_init_data(config, data, len - 1)` from `config_open_for_fuzzing()`, reserving one byte outside the parser's logical span, but Stage 02 did not dynamically validate the fixed image.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled fuzz buffer into parser state. `config_init_data()` binds the lexer cursor to the copied bytes in `static_data`, creating the exact span later consumed by the multiline-string scanner.
source.value_from: The saved vulnerable run read 70,642 bytes from `poc`, but `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` truncated that to `size = 32768` and copied the first 32,768 bytes into global `static_data`. Those copied bytes begin with `'''`, contain no `0x00` byte anywhere in offsets 0..32767, and contain no second `'''` inside the copied prefix.
source.note: At this point `lexer->pos` and `lexer->start` both point to `static_data + 0`, so the next lexer state will inspect the copied prefix starting with the opening triple quote.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: The lexer extent is materialized from the full copied length `len = 32768`, so `lexer->end` becomes `static_data + 32768`. For this witness that leaves no reserved byte between the parser's logical span and the ASan redzone, allowing the multiline-string loop to re-enter with `lexer->pos` already at the first byte past the array.
root_cause.note: The staged fix changes the fuzzing caller to pass `len - 1`, which would make `lexer->end = static_data + 32767` for this witness and prevent the extra re-entry past the end of `static_data`; Stage 02 did not dynamically validate the fixed image.

sink.description: ASan crash site. After the loop condition has advanced `lexer->pos` to `static_data + 32768`, `strncmp` reads from the first byte past the 32,768-byte global `static_data` array while probing for a closing triple-quote delimiter.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow ... READ of size 1` at `src/lib/lwan-config.c:345:14` and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of global `static_data` defined in `src/bin/fuzz/config_fuzzer.cc:44`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The fuzz harness derives the exact copied span and materializes it in the global array later named by ASan. In the saved run the 70,642-byte witness is truncated to `size = 32768`, so every byte of `static_data[0..32767]` is overwritten by attacker-controlled input before parsing begins.
tainted_value_origin.note: Direct inspection of the copied 32,768-byte prefix shows: bytes 0..2 are `'''`; there is no `0x00` byte in offsets 0..32767; the only `'''` in that prefix is the opener at offset 0; and the last copied byte `static_data[32767]` is `0x0b`.

parser_admitted.description: Because the copied prefix starts with `'''`, `lex_config()` recognizes a triple-single-quoted multiline string and dispatches into `lex_multiline_string()`.

fine_trace.note: The saved run reads 70,642 bytes from `poc`, but the harness clamps `size` to `sizeof(static_data) == 32768`. This exact truncated length becomes the parser extent later stored in `lexer->end`.

Copies the first 32,768 witness bytes into global `static_data[0..32767]`. In that copied prefix, bytes 0..2 are `'''`, there is no `0x00` byte anywhere, the only `'''` occurs at offset 0, and the last copied byte `static_data[32767]` is `0x0b`.
Source. `config_init_data()` seeds the lexer cursor from the attacker-controlled buffer, so both `lexer->pos` and `lexer->start` point at `static_data + 0`, the opening `'''` copied in step 1.

Root cause. The same initializer sets `lexer->end = static_data + 32768` from the full truncated length. For this witness that means the multiline-string loop can still execute once more after consuming the last in-bounds byte, because the logical span ends exactly at the array boundary.

The first call to `lex_config()` reads the opening quote at offset 0, then checks the next two bytes at offsets 1..2. Because step 1 established the prefix `'''`, this branch dispatches into `lex_multiline_string()`.

Because the opener was a single quote, `lex_multiline_string()` chooses the closing delimiter `end = "'''"` and advances `lexer->pos` from offset 1 to offset 3, the first byte after the opening triple quote.

There is no in-bounds closing `'''` and no NUL byte anywhere in offsets 3..32767, so the loop body never returns early and each condition call advances the cursor. On the iteration where `lexer->pos == static_data + 32767`, `next(lexer)` reads the last copied byte `0x0b`, increments `lexer->pos` to `static_data + 32768`, and returns nonzero, so the loop executes one more body iteration with `lexer->pos` already at the first byte past the array.

Sink. After step 6, `lexer->pos == static_data + 32768` while `end` is still `"'''"`. This `strncmp` probe reads from the first byte past global `static_data`, producing the saved `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow READ 1` at line 345 with stack `lex_multiline_string -> lex_next -> parse_config`.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the invalid read is 0 bytes to the right of global variable `static_data` defined here with size 32768.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_18455 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed `gt_results/arvo_18455/poc` to `/out/config_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow READ 1` in `lex_multiline_string` with stack `lex_next -> parse_config -> parser_next`.

format.name: unterminated triple-single-quoted lwan config witness truncated to a 32,768-byte parser span
format.contract: Exactly the witness stored at `gt_results/arvo_18455/poc` (70,642 bytes, sha256 `25143f39d96308035b68eea7a3e5fcad8e8593840a3bd1d74e1e0a6ee5c8b0ae`). `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` truncates it to the first 32,768 bytes before parsing. In that copied prefix, bytes 0..2 are `'''`, there is no `0x00` byte anywhere in offsets 0..32767, the only `'''` in that prefix is the opener at offset 0, and the last copied byte `static_data[32767]` is `0x0b`. Those exact witness properties make `lex_config()` enter `lex_multiline_string()`, leave the loop with `lexer->pos` advanced to `static_data + 32768`, and trigger the saved `strncmp` read one byte past global `static_data`. This contract does not claim that neighboring config inputs or other final-byte values follow the same path.
